scope: Independent read-only review of the corrected local Q24-19/Q24-20 implementation only. Do not infer whole-product, production, release or promotion readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Each durable admin operation uses its operation-specific atomic method when atomic support is declared. Partial atomic capability fails closed before request audit or mutation.

Non-atomic fallback is available only to an explicitly non-durable, non-production-safe provider whose identity mode is dev/test while the application environment is local/dev/test. Staging, production, unknown and other modes fail closed before mutation.

Tenant-scoped deactivation changes only the selected tenant/workspace membership and must not write global email, status, password hash, password_version or role_version. It remains safe if global credentials change concurrently. Other-tenant membership and session state remain intact.

Global email/password and shared role_version changes remain protected across tenants. Rejected role, grants, permission override, email or password changes leave account, memberships, sessions and outbox unchanged.

PostgresIdentityProvider.create_user either fails closed before opening a connection when no authorized actor is supplied, or delegates an actor-scoped request to the atomic admin_create_user transaction with completion outbox. The mutation/outbox transaction rolls back together.

The actual admin HTTP route is exercised through a callable atomic PostgresIdentityProvider and its returned audit event ID is present in real PostgreSQL outbox and can be projected. Clearly account for any test auth override.

The outbox projection remains idempotent and bounded, with retry/dead-letter/manual retry, consumer concurrency, worker runtime composition and restart recovery supported by implementation and test evidence. Identify material residual gaps.
